sentences.text: The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — is an incomplete postcranial skeleton lacking a skull, yet it preserves a significant portion of the vertebral column and a complete right femur.
This femur measures about 1.92 meters in length and 65 centimeters in distal width, while the spine includes nine cervical vertebrae, one dorsal vertebra, and four tail vertebrae.
Yunmenglong holds the distinction of being the first long-necked sauropod recorded from central China to date.

Estimates of its size have varied, with Paul suggesting a length of 20 meters and a weight of 30 tonnes in 2016, while Molina-Pérez and Larramendi proposed a larger length of 27 meters with a similar weight in 2020.
Fossils were discovered in the Haoling Formation within the Ruyang Basin in Henan Province, central China, and the genus was formally described in 2013 by Junchang Lü and colleagues.
Taxonomically, Yunmenglong is classified within the unranked family Somphospondyli, which serves as its parent group.
This animal lived during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately between 125 and 100 million years ago, spanning the Aptian and Albian stages in what is now Asia.
